experiments.study_type: Robotic forceps grasping at different forces and durations with tissue damage assessment
experiments.procedure_text: After thoracotomy and laparotomy, the fenestrated grasping forceps of the Saroa surgical system were used to grasp the lungs, esophagus, aorta, liver, spleen, small intestine, and large intestine
experiments.procedure_text_evidence: the fenestrated grasping forceps of the Saroa surgical system were used to grasp the lungs, esophagus, aorta, liver, spleen
experiments.animal_counts_evidence: The study used six adult male beagle dogs
experiments.test_system_evidence: Surgically resected specimens were fixed in 10% formalin

experiments.regulatory_evidence: the study is reported in accordance with ARRIVE guidelines
experiments.notes: Dogs weighed 8.06 to 9.08 kg; force–duration pairings were not specified. Two pathologists assessed tissue damage microscopically after fixation at room temperature for 24 h, paraffin embedding, and sectioning at the reported thickness of 4 mm; areas were measured using BX-analyzer.
